🇲🇽📈 BANXICO: THE ECONOMY EXPANDED IN Q2, DESPITE THE IMF'S GLOOM

The Bank of Mexico's latest minutes show the board expects the economy expanded in the second quarter after a weak start to the year, with inflation seen near 3.5% for 2026 and the reference rate held at 6.5%. Just days after the IMF cut Mexico's growth outlook to 1.2%, Banxico's own read is recovery — and the business executives it surveyed still expect gains in demand, hiring and investment over the next 12 months.

🚨🇲🇽 TAMAULIPAS LOCATED 165 MISSING PEOPLE IN ONE MONTH — 84% WITH NO CRIME

State search teams, working with the Navy, Sedena and national intelligence, located 165 missing people in Tamaulipas in June — 100 from older cases, 62 who disappeared that same month. In 84% of the cases "no crime was established," per the state prosecutor, and each person located received institutional care and immediate psychological support.

🇲🇽🌎 MEXICO INVOKES THE VIENNA CONVENTION AGAINST US PRESSURE

The SRE will keep the diplomatic notes tied to Washington's "narco" accusations against Gov. Rocha Moya, Sen. Inzunza and eight other officials classified — citing the Vienna Convention and Article 112 of the Transparency Law. Sheinbaum already ordered the extradition files opened ahead of schedule, but state-to-state diplomatic cables stay sealed. Mexico decides what it discloses, and when.

🇲🇽🌎 SAME BORDER, TWO MODELS: ICE HUNTS, MEXICO SHELTERS

Days after ICE killed another Mexican national, Welfare Secretary Ariadna Montiel toured the "Leona Vicario" migrant center in Ciudad Juárez — refuge, food, medical care and guidance for people on the move, whether heading north or returning home. The goal, she said, is "a permanent presence in the territory to guarantee direct attention to the population."

🇲🇽🇻🇪 MEXICO PULLED THEM FROM THE RUBBLE — VENEZUELA SAID THANK YOU

After Mexican soldiers deployed to Venezuela and dug survivors out of the June 24 earthquake, Caracas handed the Mexican Army three Belgian Malinois pups in gratitude. Venezuela is also sending two rescue dogs, Sol and Sara, with their handlers to train at Mexico's Military Police academy through December. Solidarity between sovereign nations — help given, help returned.

🇲🇽🏦 NU IS NOW MEXICO'S BIGGEST DIGITAL BANK

Mexico's banking regulator (CNBV) just cleared Nu to operate as a full bank. With 15+ million clients, it instantly becomes the largest digital bank in the country — started in 2019 as a single credit card, now cleared to offer payroll accounts and deposit insurance up to 3.5 million pesos. Financial inclusion at scale, under Mexican regulation.

REUTERS: Mexico's drug cartel crackdown fails to dent fentanyl flow to US, report says
July 10, 2026 | 🟡

📰 The headline says "failure." The International Crisis Group report it cites documents 2,500 arrests, 68 tons of narcotics seized, nearly 100 extraditions and up to 15,000 troops deployed to Sinaloa. 🇲🇽

The frame never asks why the world's largest fentanyl market sits north of the border, or where the cartels' guns come from — US officials themselves told researchers the flow reflects demand and shifting smuggling, not Mexican inaction.

• report concedes Mexico "scored tactical victories against criminal groups under pressure from the Trump administration"
• "no noticeable impact on fentanyl prices or availability" — attributed to US officials
